\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Decoding Boolean symbols]
\lean{Turing.decodeBool}
\label{Turing.decodeBool}
\leanok
Let $e$ be an injection from $\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ into an alphabet
$\Gamma$. For $\gamma\in\Gamma$, return the Boolean whose image under $e$ is $\gamma$,
if there is one; otherwise return no value.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Decoding an embedded Boolean]
\lean{Turing.decodeBool_apply}
\label{Turing.decodeBool_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.decodeBool}
\difficulty{4}
Let $e$ be an injective map from the Boolean set into a type with decidable equality.
Decoding the image $e(b)$ of either Boolean $b$ returns that Boolean.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Lifting an action to a larger alphabet]
\lean{Turing.Action.liftSymbols}
\label{Turing.Action.liftSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Let $e$ be an injection from the Boolean alphabet into an alphabet $\Gamma$, and let $a$
be a one-step action for a machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and state set
$S$. The corresponding action over $\Gamma$ keeps the input-head movement and successor
state, maps each written symbol and output symbol through $e$ (preserving blanks and
absent outputs), and keeps every work-head movement.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lifting a configuration to a larger alphabet]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols}
\label{Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
Let $e$ be an injection from the Boolean alphabet into an alphabet $\Gamma$, and let $c$
be a configuration with Boolean input $x$, state set $S$, and $k$ work tapes. The
resulting configuration over input $e(x)$ has the same state, input-head position, and
work-head positions; each nonblank work-tape symbol and each output symbol is mapped
through $e$, with blanks preserved.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lifting a machine to a larger alphabet]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.liftSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.decodeBool}
Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with Boolean symbols, $k$ work tapes, and state set
$S$, and let $e$ inject the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$. The machine over $\Gamma$
has the same initial state. On a transition, it decodes the input and each scanned
work-tape symbol when that symbol lies in the image of $e$ (treating all other symbols
as blank), applies the transition of $M$, and maps its written and output symbols
through $e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Scanned input symbol under symbol lifting]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols_inputSymbol}
\label{Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols_inputSymbol}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols}
\difficulty{5}
Let $e:ool	o	ext{Γ}$ be an injective map, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let
$c$ be a configuration on $x$. The symbol scanned by the input head after lifting $c$
through $e$ is the image under $e$ of the symbol scanned by $c$, with absence of a
scanned symbol preserved.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Compatibility with a change of position range]
\lean{Turing.moveInputPos_cast}
\label{Turing.moveInputPos_cast}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.moveInputPos}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers with $n+2=m+2$, let $p$ be a position in
$\{0,\ldots,n+1\}$, and let $s\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Moving $p$ by $s$ with clamping to the
valid position range and then identifying the ranges via the given equality gives the
same position as first identifying the ranges and then moving by $s$ with clamping.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lifting one computation step]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Action.liftSymbols, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols, Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols_inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.decodeBool, Turing.moveInputPos_cast}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\Gamma$ have decidable equality, let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with
Boolean symbols, and let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an
embedding. For every Boolean input word $x$ and configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, one
step of the lifted machine from the lifted configuration equals the lift of the
configuration obtained by taking one step of $M$ from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom}

Let $\Gamma$ have decidable equality, let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with
Boolean symbols, and let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an
embedding. For any Boolean input word $x$, any configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, and any
$t\in\mathbb{N}$, running the lifted machine from the lifted configuration for $t$ steps
gives the lift of the configuration reached by running $M$ from $c$ for $t$ steps.

\begin{lemma}[Lifting the initial configuration]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg}

Let $\Gamma$ be a symbol type with decidable equality, let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing

\begin{definition}[Lifting a finite machine to a larger alphabet]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols}
\label{Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols}
Let $M$ be a bundled finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, and let $e$ inject the
Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, where equality in $\Gamma$ is decidable. The resulting
finite machine over $\Gamma$ has the same number of work tapes and the same finite state
set, and uses the transition behavior obtained by decoding symbols in the image of $e$,
treating other symbols as blank, and mapping written and output symbols through $e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Lifting computation through an alphabet embedding]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols_computesFunInTimeVia}
\label{Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols_computesFunInTimeVia}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTimeVia, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Gamma$ be a type with decidable equality, let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing
machine, and let $e$ be an injection from the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$. If $M$
computes a function $f$ on Boolean words in time $T$, then the machine obtained by
lifting its symbols along $e$ computes $f$ via $e$ in time $T$: on every Boolean word
$x$ encoded letterwise by $e$, it halts within $T(|x|)$ steps and outputs the letterwise
$e$-image of $f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.decodeBool_eq_some}

\leanok

Let $e$ be an injective map from the Boolean set into a type with decidable equality,
and let $b$ be an element of that type. If decoding $b$ returns a Boolean $b$, then
$b=e(b)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mapping a buffer tape through an embedding]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_map}
\label{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_map}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{3}
Let $e$ be an injective map from the Boolean alphabet into an alphabet $\Gamma$, let $w$
be a Boolean word, and let $p$ be an integer cell. The buffer tape storing the word
obtained by applying $e$ to each symbol of $w$, at cell $p$, equals the optional symbol
on the buffer tape for $w$ at $p$ mapped through $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Decoding a mapped buffer tape]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_map_decode}
\label{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_map_decode}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.decodeBool}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Gamma$ be a type with decidable equality, let $e$ be an injective map from the
Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $p$ be an integer
cell. Reading the buffer tape for the word obtained by applying $e$ to each symbol of
$w$ at cell $p$, then decoding its symbol through $e$, gives exactly the optional symbol
on the buffer tape for $w$ at $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Lifting a configuration over another configuration]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.liftOver}
\label{Turing.Cfg.liftOver}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols, Turing.decodeBool}
Let $e$ inject the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, and let $x$ be a $\Gamma$-input and
$x'$ a Boolean input of equal length. Given a $\Gamma$-configuration $D$ on $x$ and a
Boolean configuration $c$ on $x'$, form a configuration on $x$ whose state, input-head
position, and work-head positions are those of $c$ after lifting its symbols through
$e$. At each work-tape cell, use the contents of $D$ if the contents of $c$ there equal
those of $D$ after decoding through $e$; otherwise use the lifted contents of $c$. Its
output is the output of $D$ followed by the lifted output of $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Symbol lifting commutes with a step over a configuration]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step_over}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step_over}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Action.liftSymbols, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.liftOver, Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt, Turing.decodeBool, Turing.decodeBool_eq_some, Turing.moveInputPos}
\difficulty{6}
Let $e:\\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\\to\\Gamma$ be an embedding, let $N$ be a
$k$-work-tape Turing machine with Boolean work and input symbols, and suppose its
transition action is independent of the input symbol: for every state, every two
optional input symbols, and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the actions agree. Suppose
also that no transition writes a blank on any work tape. For input words $x$ over
$\\Gamma$ and $x'$ over the Booleans of equal length, and configurations $D$ on $x$ and
$c$ on $x'$, one step of the symbol-lifted machine from the configuration obtained by
lifting $c$ over $D$ equals the configuration obtained by lifting one step from $c$ over
$D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lifting computations over a fixed configuration]
\lean{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom_over}
\label{Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom_over}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.liftOver, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step_over, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Gamma$ and $Q$ be types, let $\Gamma$ have decidable equality, and let
$e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding. Let $N$ be a
multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols and state set $Q$. Suppose its transition
action is independent of the scanned input symbol, and no transition prescribes erasing
a work-tape cell by writing a blank. Let $x$ be a $\Gamma$-word and $x'$ a Boolean word
of the same length, let $D$ be a configuration on $x$, and let $c$ be a configuration of
$N$ on $x'$. For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, running the lifted machine from the
configuration formed by lifting $c$ over $D$ for $t$ steps gives the configuration
formed by lifting the result of running $N$ from $c$ for $t$ steps over $D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Decoding a configuration's symbols]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols}
\label{Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.decodeBool}
Let $e$ inject the Boolean alphabet into $\Gamma$, where equality in $\Gamma$ is
decidable, and let $D$ be a configuration with input $x$ and state set $Q$. The
resulting Boolean configuration has an input consisting of $|x|$ copies of false, the
same state, input-head position, and work-head positions, and work-tape contents
obtained by decoding symbols through $e$ (symbols outside the image become blank). Its
output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Lifting a decoded configuration]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.liftOver_decodeSymbols}
\label{Turing.Cfg.liftOver_decodeSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols, Turing.Cfg.liftOver, Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Gamma$ and $Q$ be types, let $\Gamma$ have decidable equality, and let $e :
\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\} \hookrightarrow \Gamma$ be an injection. For every
finite input word $x$ over $\Gamma$ and every configuration $D$ with $k$ work tapes on
input $x$, lifting the configuration obtained by decoding $D$'s work-tape symbols, using
an all-false Boolean input of the same length, and then lifting its symbols via $e$
recovers $D$ exactly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise decoding of work-tape contents]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols_workTapes}
\label{Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols_workTapes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols, Turing.decodeBool}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\Gamma$ be a symbol alphabet, let $x$ be a finite
input word over $\Gamma$, and let $D$ be a configuration on $x$ with $k$ work tapes.
Given an embedding $e$ of the Boolean symbols into $\Gamma$, for every work tape $j$ and
integer cell position $p$, the decoded tape content at $(j,p)$ is the original optional
symbol at $(j,p)$ decoded to true if it equals $e(\mathrm{true})$, decoded to false if
it equals $e(\mathrm{false})$, and left blank if neither equality holds.
\end{theorem}

of the Boolean symbols into $\Gamma$, and let $x$ be a finite word over $\Gamma$. For
every configuration $D$ of a $k$-tape Turing machine with input $x$, decoding its
symbols leaves the work-tape head positions unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work tape contents under lifting]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.liftOver_workTapes}
\label{Turing.Cfg.liftOver_workTapes}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.liftOver, Turing.decodeBool}
\difficulty{1}
Let $e:ool	o	ext{Γ}$ be an injective map, and let $x$ be a finite string over $	ext{Γ}$
and $x'$ a finite Boolean string of the same length. For configurations $D$ on $x$ and
$c$ on $x'$, and for each work tape $j$ and integer tape position $p$, the symbol stored
